articles.title: Michael Strahan reportedly welcomes baby No. 5 with younger girlfriend after Isabella’s cancer battle
articles.summary: NFL News: Michael Strahan just became a dad again. Quietly. Like, really quietly. The 54-year-old \"Good Morning America\" anchor and former NFL star and his long.
articles.body: Michael Strahan just became a dad again. Quietly. Like, really quietly. The 54-year-old "Good Morning America" anchor and former NFL star and his longtime girlfriend, Kayla Quick, welcomed a baby girl earlier this year. Nobody said a word. Not Strahan, not Quick, not GMA. TMZ says it learned this from unnamed sources "with direct knowledge," so this is not confirmed by Strahan himself. No baby name, no birth date, nothing official yet. Just a report.Michael Strahan’s secret baby bombshell just opened up a whole new mystery about his longtime girlfriendHere's why this is actually wild: Strahan and Quick have been together since 2015. Ten years. And in that whole decade, they've barely been photographed together. A few red carpets, one Christmas card cameo, a football game here and there, a Duke campus visit to see his daughter.That's basically the entire public record of this relationship. Compare that to how loud Strahan gets about everything else in his family. He went on Jimmy Fallon to gush about becoming a grandpa in 2024, he posted through daughter Isabella's brain cancer battle in real time, on-air, for years. This man does not usually do quiet.Except with Kayla, apparently. She's kept an even lower profile than he has.Who is Kayla Quick? Michael Strahan’s girlfriend has a little-known history now back in focusQuick, 33, runs a wellness supplement brand called FIZZNESS and studied at the University of Tampa before pursuing culinary and nutrition programs in New York.Quick has a criminal history from her teens. At 14, she was reportedly cited for disorderly conduct in her hometown of Port Charlotte, Florida. Then in May 2005, at 18, she was arrested for grand theft after she and her then-boyfriend allegedly broke into her grandmother's home and took roughly $6,000 in jewelry, according to a Charlotte County Sheriff's arrest report. The charges were reportedly dropped, though the reasons why were never made public, meaning the case never resulted in a conviction.This would be baby No. 5 for Strahan and his first with Quick. His other four: Tanita (34) and Michael Jr. (31), from his first marriage to Wanda Hutchins (1992-1996), a marriage that started when they were teenagers in Germany, where Strahan's father was stationed. And twins Isabella and Sophia (21), from his second marriage to Jean Muggli (1999-2006), a relationship that ended in dueling abuse allegations, both denied and disputed, and one of the most expensive divorce settlements in sports history at the time.There's also this wrinkle that there were split rumors swirling around Strahan and Quick recently. So either they quietly had a baby and then quietly broke up, or the "split" chatter was overblown, or there's a timeline here nobody's actually cracked yet. TMZ's report doesn't clear any of that up, and until Strahan or Quick speaks, it's genuinely unclear which version is true.So treat this as a report, not a confirmed fact, until Strahan says something himself. But if it holds up, the man just added a fifth kid to a family he's spent a decade actively shielding from the spotlight, and somehow pulled it off without a single leak, tabloid photo, or slip-up until now.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Even after finishing his 23-year NFL career, Thomas Edward Patrick Brady Jr., better known as Tom Brady, remains one of the most financially dominant figures in American football. He earns his money through contracts, endorsements, media work and business interests.Brady’s financial profile has also changed dramatically since he retired. He also has a lucrative broadcasting contract with Fox Sports and minority ownership in the Las Vegas Raiders, exposing him to the rapidly rising value of NFL franchises. His stake could be worth something, as recent Raiders transactions indicate.Thomas Edward Patrick Brady Jr. net worth in 2026Celebrity Net Worth estimates Brady’s net worth to be $350 million, making him one of the richest former NFL players. Parade reported he earned about $333 million in salary and bonuses during his playing days with the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.Wealth sourceEstimated figure2026 estimated net worth$350 millionNFL career earnings$333 millionFox Sports contract$375 million over 10 yearsRaiders ownership5% minority stakeHe made his NFL money over two decades with the Patriots before three seasons with the Buccaneers. Celebrity Net Worth reports that Brady made approximately $235.2 million while playing for the New England Patriots and $97.8 million while playing for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.Tom Brady’s wealth and career earningsBrady’s fortune started with his playing career, although his contract strategy was often different from that of the NFL’s highest-paid quarterbacks. He spent 20 seasons with the New England Patriots before signing with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020.The basis of his wealth is an estimated $333 million in career NFL earnings. Celebrity Net Worth reports that he earned $97.8 million during his time in Tampa Bay, including $39.4 million in 2021.Tom Brady’s Raiders ownership stake gains valueBrady’s financial portfolio took a big turn when he became a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders. Reports put the franchise’s value around $9.9 billion in a 2026 transaction, and Brady’s 5% stake is estimated on paper at around $495 million. Celebrity Net Worth says that figure is the value of the stake, not cash Brady has received.Tom Brady’s broadcasting deal boosts his fortuneBrady’s move to the broadcast booth created another big financial opportunity. Fox Sports reportedly signed him to a 10-year, $375 million deal to be its lead NFL analyst, which is one of the richest sports broadcasting deals ever reported, according to Celebrity Net Worth.Celebrity Net Worth reports that the deal is worth an average of $37.5 million per year, offering Brady a long-term income stream that will carry him well past his playing career.Therefore, Brady’s financial strategy now goes beyond football pay. His NFL legacy, his broadcasting deal, commercial partnerships, and equity in the Raiders have combined to turn him from a retired quarterback into a major sports-business figure.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Robert Saleh Calls Out 'Cheap' Hit By Bears' Woods on Wan'Dale Robinson After Titans WR's Injury
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh wasn't a fan of Chicago Bears safety Xavier Woods' hit on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson that resulted in an injury during a joint practice between the two teams on Thursday.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh wasn't a fan of Chicago Bears safety Xavier Woods' hit on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson that resulted in an injury during a joint practice between the two teams on Thursday.

"It was cheap," Saleh said, per ESPN's Turron Davenport .

Near the end of practice, Robinson caught a pass from Cam Ward across the middle of the field before he was hit by Woods.

The collision led to a scuffle involving players from both teams.

While Robinson was able to get up and walk off the field under his own power, Saleh confirmed that he was being evaluated for a concussion.

Titans left guard Peter Skoronski also called out the hit by Woods after practice.

"That's Teach Tape 101 in terms of what not to do in a thud practice and a thud period," Skoronski said, per Davenport. "You can't have guys like Wan'Dale going down like that, and hits like that aren't necessary. I get we're being competitive. I get DBs are physical and stuff like that, but that's totally uncalled for in a practice thing like this. We defend our teammates, man. I don't encourage throwing punches or fighting or anything like that, but if cheap shots are taken on our guys, it's unacceptable for us."

Robinson is expected to operate as a key piece of Tennessee's passing attack this season after signing a four-year, $78 million contract with the team in free agency.

During his 2025 campaign with the New York Giants, he hauled in 92 receptions for a career-high 1,014 yards while finding the end zone four times.

As for Woods, he joined the Bears on Aug. 7 after recording 39 tackles and three passes defended across 11 games as a member of the Titans last season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce scored another major business win as his 400% growth fuels a powerful Hollywood expansion
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce has been building a life beyond the NFL, and his latest business move showed just how far that reach had grown. In October 2025, the Kans.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has been building a life beyond the NFL, and his latest business move showed just how far that reach had grown. In October 2025, the Kansas City Chiefs star’s connection to Garage Beer took an unexpected turn toward Hollywood. A new Predator-themed project featuring his brother Jason Kelce helped put the fast-growing beer brand in the spotlight while adding another layer to Travis’ expanding entertainment and business portfolio.Travis Kelce’s Garage Beer partnership gets a Hollywood boostThis story was first reported on October 31, 2025, making it last year’s news rather than a current development. At the time, Garage Beer was enjoying a major surge after Travis and Jason Kelce became investors and public faces of the brand in 2024.The attention grew even more when Jason appeared alongside former Philadelphia Eagles lineman Beau Allen in “Thermal Buzz,” a short promotional film connected to the Predator: Badlands universe. The project leaned into the brothers’ familiar humor and sports personalities while giving Garage Beer an unusual pop-culture platform.The opening line from Jason immediately set the tone: “Garage Beer saved my life.”The reference to classic 1980s action movies was more than a joke. It gave the campaign a personality that felt closely aligned with the Kelce brothers, who have built much of their public appeal around their relaxed, humorous approach.And the timing was significant for Garage Beer. According to the report, the company had seen its volume climb by more than 400% since the Kelces took stakes. Durational Capital’s investment also reportedly pushed the company’s valuation to about $200 million, while projected annual revenue had risen to between $60 million and $70 million.For Travis, the partnership highlighted a bigger trend. He was no longer simply attaching his name to brands. He was becoming part of the business story itself.Travis Kelce’s business empire stretches beyond footballThe Garage Beer investment fits neatly into the broader business strategy Travis has developed alongside his NFL career.His biggest media success has been New Heights, the podcast he hosts with Jason. What started as a sibling conversation has grown into a major entertainment platform, attracting high-profile guests and reaching audiences far beyond football. The brothers later signed a reported three-year deal with Amazon’s Wondery worth more than $100 million, further establishing their influence in sports media.Travis has also moved into traditional business ventures. He co-owns 1587 Prime, a Kansas City steakhouse with Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, and has held equity connected to Six Flags.What makes his approach particularly interesting is the variety. Football remains the foundation of Travis Kelce’s fame, but his investments increasingly connect sports, entertainment, food, media and consumer brands.The Hollywood crossover involving Garage Beer was therefore more than a promotional stunt. It reflected how the Kelce name had become a business asset capable of moving between different worlds.For an athlete still competing at the highest level, that is a striking position to reach. Travis Kelce was building the next chapter of his career while his NFL story was still being written.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Packers running back Josh Jacobs faces misdemeanor charges of battery, criminal damage to property
articles.summary: Jacobs was arrested May 26 after police were called to his home to investigate a disturbance. He was released from jail the next day.
articles.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is facing misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from what police described as a physical confrontation with his girlfriend. Jacobs was arrested May 26 after police were called to his home to investigate a disturbance and was released from jail the next day. The charges were announced Thursday by Brown County District Attorney David Lasee. “Our office sought to ensure a fair and complete review of available evidence, some of which only recently became available to our office due to significant, ongoing forensic efforts by law enforcement,” Lasee said in a statement. “A criminal complaint is nothing more than a written, formal accusation against a defendant alleging the commission of criminal offenses and does not raise any inference of guilt. Mr. Jacobs is presumed innocent of these charges. “As this is an ongoing criminal case, and out of respect for the rights of all parties, our office will not have further comment on the matter at this time.” Jacobs’ lawyers — David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III — issued a statement acknowledging the charges, noting they “do not include domestic violence.” “The allegations will be addressed in court, and not in the media,” they said. “Mr. Jacobs respects the District Attorney’s office and the process it followed.” Jacobs was back on the field with the Packers for organized team activities less than a week after the arrest and has been with the team for training camp, though he’s been limited by a groin injury. Jacobs was initially arrested on five criminal charges, including a felony count of strangulation and suffocation as well as battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct and intimidation of a victim. The only charges filed Thursday involved the misdemeanor counts of battery and disorderly conduct. Incident started with dispute over phone According to the criminal complaint, the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department responded to a report of a disturbance involving a man and a woman on the morning of May 23. Police said Jacobs’ girlfriend told them she had a lump on her head as a result of Jacobs’ actions. Police said the woman said she had been looking through Jacobs’ phone and saw he was talking to other women and that she threw the phone in anger without breaking it. She told police that Jacobs had her phone and that she told him he could look through it. Police said the woman indicated she tried to retrieve her phone from Jacobs, but he didn’t return it and instead grabbed her arm and began a struggle that lasted several minutes. Police said the two of them then left in separate vehicles, with the woman following Jacobs to try to get her phone back. They eventually returned to the home, and the woman said she was going to call police to get her phone back. Police said Jacobs called the woman a derogatory name and said he would “do something to her” as she grabbed a second phone from a duffel bag. According to police, the woman was trying to exit a garage door to get outside when Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took the phone from her while she was on the ground. Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head. According to police, the woman said Jacobs hadn’t returned her primary phone, and that her second phone was damaged as a result of the incident. According to the criminal complaint, surveillance footage from the camera system in the garage corroborated the woman’s statement. The maximum possible sentence for each of the two charges filed against Jacobs includes nine months in jail and a $10,000 fine. A Packers spokesman didn’t immediately respond to a message seeking comment Thursday. The NFL said it is monitoring the case. Loss of Jacobs would challenge Packers Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns last season. That followed a 2024 season in which Jacobs ran for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns while earning his third Pro Bowl selection. The 28-year-old has rushed for 7,803 yards and 74 touchdowns in his seven-year career, which included five seasons with the Raiders. He earned All-Pro honors and had an NFL-leading 1,653 yards rushing with Las Vegas in 2022. Running back is a position in which the Packers don’t have much depth. Injuries have caused 2024 third-round draft pick MarShawn Lloyd to play just one game over the past two seasons, though he has been healthy throughout training camp. Pierre Strong Jr. spent last season on Green Bay’s practice squad but has 499 career yards rushing with the New England Patriots (2022) and Cleveland Browns (2023-24). Chris Brooks ran for 106 yards on 27 carries last season while contributing primarily on special teams. During a news conference Wednesday, Green Bay general manager Brian Gutekunst was asked if the Packers would need to add another running back in the event Jacobs faced charges and got suspended. “Yeah, I’m pretty confident we can sustain it, but it doesn’t mean we wouldn’t do that,” Gutekunst said about adding a player. “We’ll deal with that when that comes, but we’ve obviously prepared for that in case that happens. But at the same time, I feel really good about the guys we’ve got in that room, and I think we can survive that.”

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ $325 million Kansas City Current investment has a deeper meaning as he opens up about his daughter and women’s sports
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has already changed the sporting landscape in Kansas City through his success with the Chiefs. But his ambitions have never stopped at.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has already changed the sporting landscape in Kansas City through his success with the Chiefs. But his ambitions have never stopped at football. In 2024, Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes stepped into women’s soccer ownership with the Kansas City Current, a move that reflected both their belief in the city and their desire to help create bigger opportunities for women athletes.Patrick Mahomes explains his Kansas City Current ownership decisionThis story was originally reported in March 2024, so it reflects Mahomes’ views at that time rather than a new 2026 development. The timing was significant because the Kansas City Current were preparing for their first game at CPKC Stadium, the first stadium in the world built specifically for an NWSL team.Ahead of that historic opening, Mahomes appeared on ESPN’s SportsCenter with Brittany and spoke about the excitement surrounding the new club. The atmosphere reminded him of the energy he regularly experienced at Arrowhead Stadium.“It’s been remarkable to be in the stadium and see the fans. I feel like I’m at Arrowhead, that’s the type of vibe I’m getting here. It’s going to be a historic day and the start of something great,” he said.But the decision to become part of the Current was about more than adding another investment to his growing portfolio. Mahomes connected the project to something much more personal.“Yeah, I just want to give back in the best way possible and to be making history in women’s sports, I have my own daughter, to give them the platform that they deserve. I mean, I’ve seen the type of talent they showcase every single game and we wanted to build a stadium that matched that talent. And to have it here in Kansas City as the first women’s-specific stadium, and it’s just the start of something that will kinda take off throughout the rest of the world.”That explanation offered a glimpse into what the ownership role meant to Mahomes. He was not simply buying into another professional sports franchise. He saw the Current as part of a larger opportunity to raise the profile of women’s soccer and give elite players a venue that matched their ability.Patrick Mahomes’ growing Kansas City sports ownership portfolioThe Current also became another piece of Mahomes’ remarkable connection with Kansas City sports.By 2024, the Chiefs quarterback had ownership interests in three major professional teams in the city. Along with the Current, he had invested in Sporting Kansas City and the Kansas City Royals. That put him in a rare position among active athletes, allowing him to contribute to several sports while continuing to build his own legacy on the football field.Mahomes also explained why Kansas City itself made those investments appealing.“For me, it just shows how much support Kansas City has. You go to any game, you see the fanbase and how much support,” explained Mahomes. “They really love the players for what they do on the field, but also off of it as well. It’s a great city. It’s the place me and Brittany want to raise our kids in, and it speaks to the people in this city.”That final point may be the heart of his ownership strategy. Mahomes has become one of Kansas City’s biggest sporting stars, but his investment choices suggest he wants his influence to extend beyond touchdowns and championships.His involvement with the Kansas City Current showed that legacy can take another form: helping build something that gives a new generation of athletes a bigger stage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New Rumors on Falcons QB1 Battle with Tua Losing 'Big-Time Lead' over Michael Penix Jr.
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa has lost an edge over Michael Penix Jr. in the battle for the Atlanta Falcons' starting quarterback job, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Tua Tagovailoa has lost an edge over Michael Penix Jr. in the battle for the Atlanta Falcons' starting quarterback job, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

"Tua Tagovailoa had a big-time lead in this race," Rapoport reported during a Thursday appearance on NFL GameDay (0:15 mark). "Really was his for the taking. That was the hope of the organization. That he would come in, play well, take the starting job and kind of move forward that way. Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr. could just rehab, recover from that torn ACL, get back whenever healthy, then they would reassess at some point in the season if a change needed to be made."

"Tua has been inconsistent in practice, was inconsistent in the game," he added. "Seems like he has been practicing better the last couple of days, but the door is open for Michael Penix."

Tagovailoa signed a one-year contract with the Falcons in March after serving as the Miami Dolphins' starter from 2020-25.

He received plenty of opportunities to work with Atlanta's first-team offense, as Penix was sidelined throughout the beginning of training camp while he recovered from a torn ACL that he suffered after starting nine games for the Falcons last year.

Penix wasn't fully cleared to practice until Saturday.

Still, Tagovailoa wasn't able to gain separation atop Atlanta's depth chart.

During the Falcons' preseason opener, he mishandled a snap on his first drive and only finished 3-of-5 for 22 yards through two possessions. He's also experienced his fair share of struggles during joint practices.

Tagovailoa will have another opportunity to make his case for the Falcons' starter under center in their preseason finale, as he's set to open the contest.

Penix won't make an appearance despite being cleared.

Atlanta will face the Miami Dolphins on Friday at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Prosecutor says he has portion of Josh Jacobs' domestic incident with ex-girlfriend on video
articles.summary: Surveillance video from Josh Jacobs' garage allegedly corroborates his ex-girlfriend's account of the battery, raising questions about his NFL future.
articles.body: The District Attorney who charged Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs with two domestic misdemeanors on Thursday initially released a statement about reviewing new available evidence, and now we know that evidence is surveillance video related to the alleged battery. After police investigated the incident at the scene of Jacobs' alleged battery on his ex-girlfriend, they later did more legwork according to District Attorney David L. Lasee. And they uncovered a security camera in Jacobs' garage where he and his ex-girlfriend allegedly had a physical altercation. JOSH JACOBS FACES TWO MISDEMEANOR CHARGES AFTER MAY ARREST The incident report from Lasee's office says ANM, as they are identifying the player's ex-girlfriend, told officers as she was trying to exit the garage door to get outside, "Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground and she struck her head, suffering an injury," the report reads. "Jacobs then took her phone from her while she was on the ground. ANM laid on the ground for a while and then struggled to walk back into the house." ATTORNEY FOR DENVER BRONCOS DEFENDER JONATHON COOPER PLAYS RACE CARD IN DOMESTIC ABUSE CASE Lasee's incident report says this is on video. The "surveillance footage from the camera system within the garage of the Tretni Mar residence from May 23, 2026, between 8:30 a.m. and 8:38 a.m. corroborates the relevant portions of ANM's statement that one would expect to have seen on video, including both ANM and Jacobs departing the residence in their respective vehicles and returning to the residence, as well as their actions on the security camera in the garage. "The surveillance video further shows Jacobs took ANM's phone while she was on the floor of the garage, and approximately 40 seconds later, Jacobs returns to the garage and appears to damage ANM's phone." The video is not available for independent inspection at this time. It will obviously be used as evidence in the case against Jacobs. BRONCOS STAR SPEAKS OUT FOLLOWING DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ARREST, FIRES OFF AN APOLOGY He was charged Thursday with one count of misdemeanor battery and one count of criminal damage to property. Jacobs turned himself in to police on May 26, three days after the incident at his Hobart, Wisconsin home. So far, the case has been tried in the court of public opinion as a he-said versus she-said account, with Jacobs enlisting a legal team that claims he will be exonerated of the allegations. But if the District Attorney's office indeed has a video that prosecutors say shows Jacobs getting physical with his ex-girlfriend in that garage, his legal situation will be much worse and his status as an NFL player could be at risk. The NFL, which studies practices, meetings, and games on tape, obviously frowns upon video of a battery by one of its employees and has a history of separating from such episodes. Ray Rice's career ended when a 2014 video of him striking his then-fiancée, Janay Palmer, in the face during an argument became public. The video Lasee viewed before deciding to charge Jacobs comes with its own backstory outlined in the DA's incident report: "Your complainant reviewed a follow up report from Investigator Van Lanen of the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department received on August 6, 2026, and a digital forensic examination report prepared by Frank Angel for the Brown County Sheriff’s Office, received on August 13, 2026. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "Those reports relate an on or about July 27 and 28, 2026, of recovered electronic devices from Jacobs’s residence, including components of a video surveillance system, as well as cellular phones from both Jacobs and ANM. "Angel’s report outlines the process used to conduct the forensic exam of the devices, and explained that the recovery of video files from the surveillance system was complex and took several weeks, culminating in a final verification on July 21, 2026. "Based on the foregoing, the complainant believes this complaint to be true and correct." The Packers released a statement about Thursday's charges. "We are aware of the charges brought against Josh Jacobs," the team said in a statement. "We will continue to cooperate with the NFL as we work through the process. We will have no further comment at this time." The NFL's investigation of the entire episode is ongoing and Jacobs is subject to discipline under the Personal Conduct Policy and may even be placed on the commissioner's exempt list, which would mean he'd get paid but cannot play. articles.title: Broncos coach Sean Payton buries Geoff Schwartz after analyst butchers Bo Nix's downfield game
articles.summary: Sean Payton fired back at analyst Geoff Schwartz after his claim that Bo Nix doesn't push the ball downfield was corrected by deep-ball stats.
articles.body: Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton has little patience for careless sports TV analysis, especially from former NFL players who should know what goes into evaluating a quarterback. So when former offensive lineman-turned-TV analyst Geoff Schwartz mischaracterized Bo Nix on national television this week, Payton responded directly. Schwartz appeared Wednesday on "First Things First" as the panel debated whether Nix was primed for a major second-year jump or likely to level off. Schwartz argued Nix was still essentially the same quarterback he had been in college. NO, LAMAR JACKSON DOESN'T DESERVE TO BE RANKED AMONG THE NFL'S TOP 10 QUARTERBACKS "I do think he just is what he is at this point. He looks like the same quarterback he was in college... He's consistent. He's not gonna make mistakes. But he's not gonna push the ball down the field all that often." The clip quickly drew a Community Note correcting Schwartz’s claim: Nix has thrown the most touchdown passes of 20-plus air yards in the NFL since the start of the 2024 season, with 19 including the postseason ... That makes Schwartz’s assessment difficult to defend. Nix may not be a finished product, and questions about his long-term ceiling are fair. But claiming he does not push the ball downfield ignores how Denver has used him. BRONCOS STAR QUARTERBACK BO NIX UNDERWENT SECOND PROCEDURE ON SURGICALLY REPAIRED ANKLE: REPORT Payton caught Schwartz's take and brutally offered his own assessment. "Always easy to tell who works at it and who doesn't," Payton said, responding to Schwartz. Payton quoted the post and went straight at the work behind Schwartz’s take. Former players are hired to provide perspective beyond standard debate-show talking points. That is why Schwartz’s claim stood out. Nix’s deep-ball production is not an obscure or cherry-picked statistic. It directly contradicts the premise of Schwartz’s take. Schwartz may believe Nix has limitations as a passer. That is a fair discussion. But presenting him as a limited quarterback who rarely attacks downfield is not supported by the numbers. Schwartz got sacked, plain and simple. articles.title: Tony Romo receives 3 new citations following OWI arrest in Milwaukee
articles.summary: Romo is due in court on Sept. 21. It's unclear if he'll call games for CBS Sports again.
articles.body:
Tony Romo has received three new citations stemming from his arrest in Milwaukee on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated, according to the Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel .

According to online court records, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and current CBS Sports analyst was cited for first-offense operating while intoxicated, unsafe passing on the right side and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle. Romo had already received a citation on July 27 for refusing to take an intoxication test after his arrest.

Romo is reportedly due in court for all four citations on Sept. 21.

His camp also released a new statement to the Journal-Sentinel:

"Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps."

Romo was arrested on July 23 after being pulled over on a Milwaukee highway and performing poorly on a field sobriety test, according to police.

Romo was once the darling of NFL media and CBS paid him like it with a record-shattering 10-year, $180 million contract in 2020. His luster had worn off considerably even before the arrest, with his meandering and casual commentary style wearing thin for many fans .

So it might not be a surprise if CBS uses the arrest to get out of that contract and cut Romo loose. The Athletic noted his contract contains a morals clause that could allow CBS to void the deal if he embarrasses the company.

In the meantime, CBS is set to open the season with J.J. Watt working opposite Jim Nantz in its No. 1 booth.

articles.title: Dillon Gabriel, an afterthought in Browns' QB competition, has a fantastic preseason finale
articles.summary: Dillon Gabriel had a very efficient night against the Patriots.
articles.body:
Dillon Gabriel never really made a move in the Cleveland Browns' quarterback competition this preseason. Maybe he was never given a true shot.

Deshaun Watson was the QB1 most of the offseason, and when the Browns picked him as the starter it seemed like a predetermined outcome. Shedeur Sanders was the one who was said to have been competing with Watson. He got a start in the Browns' second preseason game ahead of Watson.

Gabriel, a third-round pick last year, never seemed like a consideration. That made Thursday night's performance a bit interesting.

Gabriel had a big first half for the Browns in the preseason finale against the New England Patriots as Watson and Sanders sat out. Gabriel was 12 of 15 for 186 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions in the first half. His 157.9 passer rating was just short of a perfect mark, which is 158.3. The Browns scored on all five of Dillon's possessions in the first half, not counting a one-play drive before the half expired.

Watson was an unpopular pick as the Browns' starter for Week 1. Sanders didn't do enough to clearly win the job. There will be some wondering if Gabriel should have gotten a longer look, especially since Thursday night's game happened on a national Amazon Prime Video broadcast.

"What a great half, happy for him," Browns coach Todd Monken said during an Amazon Prime Video interview at halftime. "Guys played well around him. Certainly took advantage of his opportunity."

Thursday night's performance highlighted what Gabriel does well. He understands where to go with the ball, makes quick decisions and can accurately deliver short passes to playmakers. He doesn't have a cannon arm and won't often push the ball downfield, but he did roll out for one intermediate completion that turned into a 52-yard gain.

All of Gabriel's touchdowns were similar. They were quick passes that found the open spot in the defense and allowed the target to get into the end zone.

The Browns have made their decision with Watson and aren't going to turn back from it. But Cleveland is also likely to have multiple starting quarterbacks this season. Gabriel made his case to be one of those quarterbacks, if the situation arises.

articles.title: Drew Allar, Will Howard Struggle in QB3 Battle, Box Score Stats & Highlights from Steelers vs. Bills
articles.summary: Drew Allar and Will Howard were both under center for the Pittsburgh Steelers during the team's 28-27 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Drew Allar and Will Howard were both under center for the Pittsburgh Steelers during the team's 28-27 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night.

Howard played the first half of the game before Allar took the field for the second half, although neither player was able to truly stand out.

Here's a closer look at how they performed.

Former NFL QB has theory about Browns' QB pick

The Steelers' first possession of the game with Allar on the field was a successful one, as they opened the third quarter with a 68-yard drive that was capped off by a nine-yard rushing touchdown from running back Eli Heidenreich.

Pittsburgh wasn't able to move the chains as easily afterwards, as the team's next two drives ended with punts.

The Steelers advanced into Bills territory on Allar's fourth drive, but couldn't convert on fourth down with four yards to gain at Buffalo's 41-yard line.

After the Bills took a late one-point lead, Pittsburgh received the ball with an opportunity to move back in front. The Steelers recorded another turnover on downs after a fourth-down pass from Allar fell incomplete, though.

As for Howard, he finished with a pair of touchdown passes before getting picked off in the second quarter.

He put Pittsburgh on the board with a touchdown off a screen pass to rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard in the first quarter before connecting with tight end Lake McRee for another short score later in the quarter.

While the Steelers led 14-10 at halftime, it's worth noting that their offense wasn't able to consistently move down the field with Howard.

They finished with just 98 total yards in the first half.

As Aaron Rodgers remains the unquestioned starter in Pittsburgh, Allar and Howard continued their battle for positioning on the Steelers' depth chart.

articles.title: Tony Romo hit with several new citations after OWI arrest, further jeopardizing return to NFL broadcasts
articles.summary: Tony Romo faces three new Milwaukee citations including operating while intoxicated and open intoxicants tied to his July arrest on a highway.
articles.body: Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo made headlines in July when he was arrested on charges of allegedly operating a vehicle while intoxicated. Romo was stopped on a highway, then did not perform well when given field sobriety tests by police. He was released, and is supposed to appear in court in September. Almost immediately afterward, CBS Sports announced that they would put him on leave from broadcasting duties "until further notice." Now, he's facing several additional citations in Milwaukee related to that arrest, per a new report from the New York Post. According to newly filed court records, Romo now faces "first-offense operating while intoxicated, unsafe passing on the right side, and possessing open intoxicants inside his vehicle," the report says. TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT A spokesperson for Romo issued a statement saying that he "accepts full responsibility" for what happened and reiterating that it’s a civil, not criminal, matter. "Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps." After the arrest, many speculated that his time in the CBS broadcast booth may be over. Boomer Esiason said it’s likely he’ll have to move on and get things "straightened out." BODYCAM SHOWS TONY ROMO ARGUING WITH OFFICER BEFORE REFUSING BREATH TEST DURING DUI ARREST "If I had to guess, purely speculation given what’s going on right now, I would think it’s over," Esiason said on WFAN. "He may end up going somewhere else and getting things straightened out." CBS Sports president David Berson said recently that it's still an "evolving situation" and that it's unclear when, or if, Romo ever returns to the booth with CBS. "It’s an evolving situation and therefore we are still assessing," Berson explained. "There is no timetable or final decision at this time." "I hope you can respect and appreciate this is a personnel matter and a legal one for Tony, so I can’t speak to that aspect of things," he said. articles.title: Rookie QB Ty Simpson has another efficient game as Rams wrap up preseason
articles.summary: Stetson Bennett IV has apparently won the Rams' QB2 job.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams rookie quarterback Ty Simpson might not play much or at all this regular season, but the Rams should feel good about what they saw from him in the preseason.

Simpson, the No. 13 overall pick of this year's NFL Draft, completed a ton of passes Thursday night as he completed what has to be considered a successful preseason. Simpson played a half and completed 18 of 23 passes for 119 yards and a touchdown. It was a similar stat line to his first preseason game, when he completed 21 of 25 passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Despite the good stats in the preseason, it appears Simpson is set for a redshirt rookie season.

Unless there are some injuries or changes to the depth chart, Simpson might not play this season. It appears he will begin his career as the Rams' third-string quarterback behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett IV. Simpson got the start Thursday while the other two rested. That's a strong indication that Bennett has locked up the Rams' backup quarterback job. It's rare for a quarterback drafted as high as Simpson to be on the third team at the beginning of the season, but that's how it appears Simpson's NFL career will start. Though, Simpson's preseason performances at least might give the Rams' staff something to consider when it comes to the No. 2 quarterback job, either heading into the season or shortly into it.

On Thursday night Simpson completed most of his passes, which he has done through the preseason. He has shown he is capable of quick reads and delivering short passes with good timing and accuracy. Simpson completed 12 of his first 13 passes but none of the completions went for more than 10 yards.

Most of Simpson's preseason has been taking what the defense gives him and doing it quickly. The next step in his progression will be taking smart chances downfield when opportunities arise. That's a reason he will be developing while not playing this season. It was still a productive preseason, which ended with Simpson completing 47 of 60 passes (78.3%) for 382 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

There were some missed opportunities at an even bigger night for Simpson and the offense. The Rams got the ball at the Chargers' 14-yard line after a fumble but managed just 5 yards and a field goal. Later the Rams drove to the 1-yard line but were stuffed on consecutive runs on third and fourth down. Those failures are far from being all Simpson's fault, but it would have looked better had those drives ended with touchdowns.

Simpson's best play of the night, and perhaps his best play of the preseason, came on the Rams' first touchdown. Feeling pressure he escaped the pocket to his left. Moving that way, he turned his body while on the move and made a nice throw to Brennan Presley for the score. That play showed a lot of athleticism, which was a reason Simpson was a high pick.

Bennett has been ahead of Simpson all offseason in the race to be Stafford's backup, and Bennett played well enough in the preseason that he hasn't lost any ground. Apparently head coach Sean McVay had seen enough because Bennett sat out Thursday while Simpson played. One of the knocks on Simpson coming out of college was he didn't have much experience. He had 15 starts at Alabama, all of which came last season. Being able to sit and learn is probably good for his development. The Rams hope they don't need any quarterback other than Stafford this season.

Rams fans got a look at Simpson, their presumed quarterback of the future, this preseason. If everything goes right, their next chance to watch him play will come next preseason.

images.caption: Quarterback Ty Simpson got the start in the Rams' preseason finale. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill) (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill)
